children.text:
This site will be devoted above all to the old Slavic hillforts located in the territory of Slovakia, but we will not avoid Slavic hillforts in other countries, or the hillforts of other cultures, especially the Celts and the Lusatian culture.
  I am not a professional historian, but I have been interested in the history of the Slavs for a long time alongside my other duties, so please be indulgent.  I have found that there is no website devoted to the old hillforts in the way there is, for example, for castles and manor houses. Information about individual hillforts can indeed be found, but it is fairly laborious and time-consuming. My intention is to create a site with as many Slavic hillforts as possible, and for each hillfort I would like to assemble the most comprehensive information available today. This will cover the presently known history of the hillfort, the finds, drawings, reconstructions, photographs and so on. I would most of all like to get down to the absolute foundations – that is, to the actual works of the archaeologists who investigated the hillforts in the past. That, however, is the ideal state I would like to achieve, and I am well aware that such a goal cannot be reached in 1–2 months; it is a long-term matter.

To begin with I will put up a few hillforts that I have managed to work my way through so far, and further hillforts and more detailed information on the existing ones will be added gradually.  Many of the articles you will read here will be taken from other authors, or from other sites where information about hillforts is scattered; in such cases the source will of course always be given. Should any author not wish his article to appear on this site, I will of course accept that and delete it, but I hope I will not have to deal with such problems and that people will understand that this is a non-profit blog which seeks, with good intentions, to inform the public and to awaken interest in our shared glorious history.  If archaeologists and historians also find their way to this site and wish to add or correct something, I shall be very glad to be instructed.

Slavic hillforts are not only a symbol of the great building skill of our Slavic ancestors, who more than 1000 years ago were able to build mighty fortifications before which even the greatest armies of their day more than once capitulated, but they are also living proof of their independence, sophistication, pride, wealth and political power. The hillforts were home to our magnates and their families, to the military retinue, but also to skilled craftsmen – smiths and jewellers, whose products we can admire to this day thanks to archaeology – to merchants, to the clergy and to other important inhabitants. Besides the buildings of the ordinary population, at hillforts we find the representative dwellings of the nobility, the first Christian churches and pagan sanctuaries.  
  Another aim of the site is to bring readers, in an engaging form, closer to an extraordinarily interesting period of our national history – the Early Middle Ages, especially in the time of Great Moravia. Let us be proud of our history. We have many reasons to be.
